mechanism: Train a propensity-score model e(x)=P(treatment|covariates) on randomly assigned train/control splits; stratify the sample into propensity bins (or IPW-reweight); within bins where misclassification of buy/sell labels dominates, mark bad samples and train final classifiers only on well-responding strata—so propensity strata act as a sensor of which covariate neighborhoods are currently 'trainable' vs confounded (explicitly including high vs low volatility neighborhoods as confounders).
data_needed: Labeled buy/sell features X, treatment assignment T, CatBoost (or logistic) PSM probabilities, bin edges (e.g. 0.3–0.7 or IPW-transformed scores), bad-sample book from stratum error counts.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Forex time-series classification (volatility-heterogeneous examples); OOS trading charts shown; no single symbol/TF locked in text.
why_new_for_mis: Turns causal propensity strata/IPW into a live heterogeneity/regime sensor: which market neighborhoods are currently estimable vs should be gated off—not just a training trick.
quote: in Forex, each individual training example may belong to the area of high or low volatility

mechanism: Instead of treatment propensity, train one classifier on target labels, bin predicted probabilities into strata, and gate training/trading by discarding strata where incorrect predictions (× coefficient) exceed correct ones—a probability-mass quality sensor for current market states.
data_needed: Classifier propensity-to-label probabilities, bins_number, lower_bound/upper_bound (e.g. 0.3–0.7), coefficient threshold, labeled outcomes.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Same Forex classification setup as above; 25-model ensembles with OOS balance charts.
why_new_for_mis: Gives MIS a soft 'predictability mass' sensor over probability bins rather than hard price regimes.
quote: for strata where the number of incorrectly guessed (multiplied by a ratio) examples exceeds the number of correctly guessed ones, the condition for adding bad examples to the book of bad examples is triggered

mechanism: Build meta_X from rolling std columns of price features; cluster with HDBSCAN/KMeans/BIRCH/GMM; train a specialized CatBoost meta-model to predict cluster membership from volatility features and a main model only on filtered labels within each regime—yielding discrete volatility market modes (sideways vs spike/trend-change).
data_needed: Price features excluding 'std' for main model; 'std' volatility meta-features; cluster labels; EURUSD history with PERIODS and PERIODS_META.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD; H1 example; train window BACKWARD=2019-01-01 to FORWARD=2023-01-01; PERIODS 10..90 step 10; PERIODS_META=[20]; n_clusters up to 40.
why_new_for_mis: Explicit volatility-driven unsupervised regime sensor with per-regime models—HDBSCAN preferred because it needs no preset cluster count.
quote: Clustering can also be viewed in terms of identifying market regimes, for example based on volatility.

mechanism: KMeans-cluster feature space; within each cluster separately tally buy/sell mislabels across ensemble meta-learners; mark recurrent bad indices per cluster then train only on cleaned labels—localizing treatment-effect heterogeneity and reducing OOS balance noise when market structure shifts across clusters.
data_needed: Feature matrix X, KMeans cluster ids, BAD_CLUSTERS per buy/sell, bad_samples_fraction threshold.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Same EURUSD H1 causal-clustering pipeline; ONNX-exportable models.
why_new_for_mis: Uses clustering as a matching sensor so regime-local error structure—not global averages—gates which states remain tradable after a regime shift.
quote: Experiments have shown that taking into account bad trades using clustering reduces the range of values (the balance curve becomes smoother) and improves the model's capability to predict on new data.

mechanism: Collect last time_step OHLC bars, reshape into a (1, time_step, features) tensor matching training get_sequential_data, apply the identical saved StandardizationScaler (and optional PCA), then run ONNX LSTM to emit bullish/bearish class—enforcing train/serve parity for a sequential pattern sensor.
data_needed: OHLC rates (e.g. 7-bar window), saved mean/std (and PCA components), ONNX LSTM, class vector {0,1}.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD; PERIOD_D1 for data/model; realtime EA also run on H1 chart with D1 rates; optional H12 tester.
why_new_for_mis: Specifies the exact live sequential tensor + frozen scaler/PCA contract needed to treat an LSTM as a reliable MIS neural sensor rather than a one-off Python notebook.
quote: You still need to define a time window of past data for the model to consider when making predictions.

mechanism: Screen symbol universe with |Pearson|>0.8 and Engle–Granger cointegration p<0.05 on daily closes; maintain a rolling Pearson indicator on BarsBack closes as a live pair-relationship strength sensor before enabling arb.
data_needed: Daily closes for filtered symbols (EUR*/USD*/crypto/NASDAQ CFDs); scipy pearsonr + statsmodels coint; MQL5 Pearson.mq5 buffer.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Many FX/crypto pairs on D1 (e.g. EURUSD–USDBGN); teaching pair NZDUSD–AUDUSD D1; NASDAQ #AMZN–#NFLX D1; Pearson on PERIOD_CURRENT with BarsBack=100.
why_new_for_mis: Gives MIS a tradable-pair eligibility/relationship sensor from cointegration+correlation that can gate other signals when the link breaks.
quote: if abs(corr) > 0.8:  # Correlación fuerte ... if p_value < 0.05:

mechanism: Two Conv1D+LSTM ONNX close-forecast models (120-bar MinMax history) produce predicted prices; compare predicted spread vs current spread and vs mean±2σ of stored spreads to trigger mean-reversion entries—sensing when realized pair dislocation exceeds forecast-implied equilibrium.
data_needed: Per-leg SAMPLE_SIZE=120 D1 closes, ExtMin/ExtMax normalize, dual ONNX outputs, rolling spreads[] std.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: NZDUSD+AUDUSD D1 models traded on M1 tester; #AMZN+#NFLX D1; sample_size 120*20 or 120*25*3.
why_new_for_mis: Combines neural price forecasts with a cointegrated-spread dislocation sensor—MIS can treat forecast-vs-realized spread gap as a change cue.

mechanism: Label future SMA_5 vs SMA_50 relation at look_ahead=20 bars; TimeSeriesSplit-compare classifiers predicting that crossover vs raw close direction; LDA dominates crossover task while failing on price—so forecast the MA regime state rather than tick direction, enriched with MACDh and AO after backward selection.
data_needed: EURUSD M15 OHLC+tick_volume+spread, SMA_5/SMA_50, MACDh_12_26_9, AO_5_34; LDA on selected predictors.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD; TIMEFRAME_M15; 2020-01-01 to ~2024-06; look_ahead=20 bars (~5 hours).
why_new_for_mis: Empirically motivates sensing smoothed MA-regime flips instead of raw price flips as a more stationary trend-state target for MIS classifiers.
quote: moving average crossovers may be more reliable to forecast than direct changes in price

mechanism: Place/trail SL/TP as multiples of ATR-derived min_distance×sl_width so stop geometry expands/contracts with current volatility rather than fixed pip distances.
data_needed: Symbol TRADE_STOPS_LEVEL / ATR-linked min_distance; bid/ask; open positions.
why_new_for_mis: Simple live volatility sensor for risk geometry that MIS can share across strategies.
quote: we will use the Average True Range (ATR) to calculate how wide or narrow our stops should be

mechanism: Detect trend turning points (TTPs) with min_step deviation; fit least-squares slope/intercept per bidirectional segment; emit (slope, intercept, duration/length_fraction) as a fixed-size piecewise-linear encoding of multimodal bars—dynamic segment lengths replace fixed windows as the trend-regime representation fed to MLP forecasting.
data_needed: Normalized multimodal HistoryBars×BarDescr tensor; OpenCL PLR kernel; min_step≈0.3 on normalized data.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD H1; full year 2023 training; 24-hour forecast horizon shown.
why_new_for_mis: Supplies MIS a scale-adaptive trend-segment sensor (slope+duration) instead of fixed-length bars or single MAs.
quote: the piecewise linear representation method allows the use of dynamic segment sizes, depending on the analyzed input time series

mechanism: Extract long-term temporal features (slope sm, duration dm) via PLR and short-term spatial features via CNN/CSCM over the market matrix; LSTM Encoder with feature-wise attention selects relevant short-term dims; LSTM Decoder attends over Encoder states fused with PLR long-term features to predict trend direction and duration.
data_needed: OHLCV + technical indicators market matrix; PLR δ threshold; CNN kernels 1×3..1×5; dual LSTM+attention stacks.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD H1; train 2023; test January 2024 (26 trades, PF 1.12).
why_new_for_mis: Packages short-horizon spatial microstructure and long-horizon PLR trend into one dual-attention trend-state neural sensor for MIS.
quote: TPM uses piecewise linear regression and a convolutional neural network to extract long-term and short-term market features

mechanism: Encoder: FFN-smooth multivariate Xt then continuous/masked spatial Self-Attention to extract SSAt; Decoder: FFN+masked temporal Self-Attention on target history Yt then transform-attention fusing SSAt with TSAt for multi-step forecasts—STI-style conversion of cross-variable spatial info into target temporal dynamics.
data_needed: Multivariate bar features (HistoryBars×BarDescr); target variable history length NForecast; multi-head STNN Encoder/Decoder layers.
why_new_for_mis: Separates a spatial cross-feature attention sensor from a causal temporal sensor—useful MIS building blocks even when end-to-end PF was weak in the author's fork.
quote: The spatial Self-Attention structure in the STNN collects efficient spatial information from multivariate variables, while the temporal Self-Attention structure collect information about the temporal evolution.

mechanism: Adam-mini shares one second-moment learning rate per dense Hessian block (mean of squared grads) instead of per-parameter v; implemented in OpenCL UpdateWeightsAdamMini for FC/conv layers—training optimizer engineering, not a market-state sensor.
data_needed: Model gradients/weights; block groupings (e.g. attention-head Q/K).
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Retrains TPM stack on EURUSD H1 2023; Jan 2024 test comparable to Adam.
why_new_for_mis: After full read: optimizer/memory technique only—no regime, vol, liquidity, or sequence market sensing.
quote: Adam-mini significantly reduces the number of learning rates used in Adam, which allows to reduce memory consumption by 45-50%.

mechanism: For every Market Watch symbol × {M1,M5,H1,H4,D1}, compute RSI(14, PRICE_CLOSE) each tick; color cell green if RSI<30 (oversold), red if RSI>70 (overbought), gray otherwise—forming a live cross-sectional momentum/exhaustion heat map.
data_needed: iRSI handles per symbol/TF; rsi_Data_Val[0]; Market Watch symbol list.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: All SymbolsTotal(true) Market Watch names; periods M1, M5, H1, H4, D1; RSI period 14.
why_new_for_mis: Turns classical RSI into a multi-asset multi-horizon state panel MIS can ingest as a breadth/exhaustion sensor, not a single-chart oscillator.
quote: If the RSI value is below 30, indicating an oversold condition, the button's background color will change to green. If the RSI value is above 70, indicating an overbought condition, the background color will change to red.

mechanism: Given known period w (24 on H1≈1 day), transpose/downsample length-L series into w subsequences of length L/w; shared linear/conv forecast each subsequence's inter-period trend to horizon H/w; optional 2-period conv aggregation + mean RevIN—extremely light periodicity-aware forecaster.
data_needed: Normalized HistoryBars×BarDescr; period w=24; forecast length multiple of w; SparseTSF conv+transpose stack.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD H1; train 2023; test Jan 2024 (81 trades, PF 1.33); hour-of-day PnL breakdown.
why_new_for_mis: Explicitly factors session/daily periodicity into a sparse inter-period trend sensor—MIS can reuse the w-subsequence decomposition without heavy Transformers.
quote: the original problem of forecasting time series is simplified to the problem of forecasting the interperiod trend.

mechanism: Decompose multimodal series into trend (PLR→CutTrendAndOther), seasonality (FFT→complex normalize→frequency Self-Attention selecting coherent cross-variable frequencies→iFFT), and residual; use PLR tokens as soft prompts; patch+cross-attend components then forecast each and weighted-sum—structured trend/season/noise sensors for forecasting.
data_needed: Multimodal sequence; PLR segments; FFT size power-of-two; complex freq attention; patch embeddings; cross-attention vs PLR prompts.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Financial time series architecture for the NeuroNet stack; live EURUSD results deferred to next article.
why_new_for_mis: Gives MIS an explicit three-way structural sensor (trend vs seasonal vs residual) with frequency-domain attention to pick coherent seasonal bands—beyond black-box sequence models.
quote: TEMPO first decomposes the original multimodal time series data into three components: trend, seasonality, and residuals.
